title: The CSS box model
goal: Understand the difference between inner and outer spacing.
explanation: A box has content, padding, a border and margin. Padding separates content from the border; margin creates space outside the border.
With content-box, a declared width describes the content box. Padding and borders add to the rendered width. With border-box, the declared width includes padding and borders; margin stays outside.
For predictable sizing, apply box-sizing: border-box to elements and pseudo-elements. Inspect the box-model diagram in developer tools before guessing at unexpected gaps.
exercise: Give a card 20px of inner spacing and 16px of outer spacing. Compare content-box with border-box.
hint: Inner means padding; outer means margin.

quiz.question: Which property adds space between content and its border?
quiz.explanation: Padding is inside the border. Margin separates the box from surrounding boxes.
